{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABi7Az5w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhMRP_M", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 154, "title": "Use compact icons for mute and fullscreen controls", "body": "## Problem

The player currently uses visible text for Mute, Fullscreen and Exit fullscreen. These common actions are readily recognizable as icons, and text consumes valuable toolbar and gameplay space on phones. The sibling snes-rust player already uses a speaker SVG and a compact fullscreen icon.

## Expected outcome

- Replace the visible Mute label with a speaker icon showing sound waves when unmuted and a crossed-out/muted speaker when muted.
- Replace Fullscreen and the touch-only Exit fullscreen control with recognizable expand and contract corner icons, respectively. Use icon-only presentation consistently on desktop and mobile.
- Keep accessible names, tooltips and state indications, and preserve the existing behavior of all three controls.
- Preserve the text labels for Play/Pause/Resume, Reset, Save and Load, the volume slider/value, and the existing player layout and gameplay-only fullscreen.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline [c6e6dea](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/commit/c6e6dea1178fefde1bfc9d99f8b3b18e0ac37b02). Inspect latest main before implementation.

- [web/index.html](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/index.html): buttons #sound, #fullscreen and #exit-fullscreen currently have visible text.
- [web/src/main.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/main.ts): refreshSound updates aria-pressed from the actual mute state; fullscreen handlers manage gameplay-only fullscreen and focus.
- [web/src/style.css](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/style.css): existing toolbar and responsive fullscreen layout. Preserve the touch-target and safe-area behavior established in #146.
- Reference: [snes-rust web/index.html](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/5fa0a3fce4add87b5342571764abb2fb7af2066a/web/index.html) and [web/style.css](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/5fa0a3fce4add87b5342571764abb2fb7af2066a/web/style.css). Its speaker SVG switches between sound waves and a mute mark. It uses a compact fullscreen icon at narrow widths; for WonderSwan, use icons at all widths.

Use small inline SVGs with currentColor and aria-hidden="true"; do not add icon libraries, fonts, dependencies or external assets. Retain semantic buttons and existing IDs. Provide descriptive accessible names and title tooltips (e.g. Mute, Fullscreen, Exit fullscreen); for mute, keep a stable toggle name with aria-pressed and an appropriate tooltip for the current action. Update the icon from the actual mute preference, including restoration on reload; do not confuse zero volume or browser audio-unlock state with explicit mute. Maintain visible focus and disabled states. Use at least 44×44 CSS pixel hit targets, not just 44px visual spacing. Keep the exit button clear of the picture and game input targets. Do not alter the existing fullscreen entry/exit, keyboard Escape, focus restoration, audio unlock or mute/volume persistence logic except as needed to update the presentation.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three buttons display clear SVG icons rather than visible text; mute switches between speaker and muted speaker on toggle and reflects the stored preference after reload. Accessible names, tooltips, aria-pressed, keyboard activation and focus remain correct.
- [ ] Existing mute/unmute behavior, slider/value and audio recovery are preserved. Fullscreen opens only the gameplay container; the touch exit icon exits it, and desktop native/Escape exit remains functional. No duplicate controls or new dependencies.
- [ ] Verify representative desktop and touch layouts at 375×812, 812×375 and 320×568 using existing fixtures and focused browser checks. Both game orientations remain usable, controls are reachable and the three icon buttons have at least 44×44 CSS pixel hit targets where displayed. Scrolling is acceptable in constrained layouts. Preserve existing layout, save-state controls and eleven-button controller; do not expand into a broader redesign.
- [ ] Update existing browser assertions as needed to check accessible names and actual state rather than visible button text. Run applicable production-preview build and browser checks (npm ci, npm run build:wasm if needed, npm run build, npm run test:browser, npm run test:compat) and git diff --check. Reuse existing coverage and builds; no Rust or fixture changes/checks are needed for a frontend-only change. Record actual results.

Keep this a small UI-only change. No human sign-off or physical phone is required. Do not introduce exhaustive viewport sweeps, pixel-level icon optimization or unrelated refactors. Merge and close once the requested behavior and applicable checks pass without a material regression.

## Optional validation

Representative before/after screenshots if useful; not a merge blocker.

## Required post-merge verification

After merge and closure, verify the Pages deployment for the merge revision and smoke-test the mute toggle, fullscreen entry and touch exit on the published player. Record the workflow URL, actual results and limitations. outputs.message:
Issue #154 is closed, and PR #155 was merged into `main`. I posted the verification results on the issue. [Issue comment](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/154#issuecomment-7208313951)

The Pages workflow succeeded for the merge commit, and the published files matched its deployment artifact byte for byte. The live player passed mute and unmute, mute persistence after reload, gameplay-only fullscreen, desktop Escape, and touch exit. Every visible icon button measured 44×44 CSS pixels in the tested layouts. The smoke test used headless Chromium on desktop and at 375×812 with touch emulation, with one ROM orientation. [Pages workflow run](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/actions/runs/45929272626)
